## Incident Report — MTA-2024-11-26 Traffic Analysis Exercise

### Victim Host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.11.26.183 |
| MAC address | d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (FQDN desktop-b8tqk49.nemotodes.health) |
| AD domain | NEMOTODES (realm NEMOTODES.HEALTH), DC = NEMOTODES-DC at 10.11.26.3 |
| Logged-in user | NEMOTODES\oboomwald — confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ exchanges with the DC (CNameString = oboomwald) and corroborated by NTLMSSP (hostname DESKTOP-B8TQK49) |

### Malware Family
**NetSupport RAT** (the commercial NetSupport Manager remote-control client, run as an unauthorized/malicious C2 agent).

Attribution is **both signature-confirmed and behaviorally confirmed**:
- Signature hits: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin`/`Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`.
- Independently verified in the raw traffic: HTTP requests to the C2 carry the literal User-Agent `NetSupport Manager/1.3`, and the exported HTTP bodies contain NetSupport's native client protocol tokens — `CMD=POLL / INFO=1 / ACK=1` (keepalive) and `CMD=ENCD / ES=1 / DATA=<encrypted blob>` (data channel) — sent as plaintext HTTP POSTs to `/fakeurl.htm`, disguised on TCP/443 (not actual TLS).

### Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — plaintext HTTP POST beacon to `/fakeurl.htm`, User-Agent `NetSupport Manager/1.3`. Beaconed roughly every 60 seconds from 04:50:45 UTC through ~05:43 UTC.

**Abused legitimate NetSupport infrastructure**
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` → 104.26.1.231, 104.26.0.231, 172.67.68.212 — `GET /location/loca.asp`, returned GPS coordinates `33.7488,-84.3877` (Atlanta, GA area), used by the RAT client to geolocate the victim.

**Delivery/lure chain** (immediately precedes first C2 check-in by ~30 seconds):
- `classicgrand.com` → 213.246.109.5:443 (first contact 04:50:11 UTC; up to 3.1 MB transferred over TLS)
- `modandcrackedapk.com` → 193.42.38.139:443 (repeated contacts 04:50:14–04:50:40 UTC; flagged by `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup` and `...in TLS SNI`; largest session transferred 5.5 MB over TLS)
- `confirmsubscription.com` → 52.8.34.0 / 13.56.30.207:443 (same time window, likely an ad/redirect hop in the same chain)
- These sessions were interleaved with benign CDN pulls (fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com, code.jquery.com, maps.googleapis.com), consistent with a rendered fake download/CAPTCHA landing page immediately before infection.

**Transferred files / hashes**
No SHA256 or filename for the dropped payload can be produced from this capture. The only bytes recoverable in cleartext (via `tshark --export-objects http`) were benign: `connecttest.txt` (MS NCSI check), `ProcessMAU.txt` (Adobe update-check response, 4 bytes), `loca.asp` (geo coordinates), and the NetSupport POLL/ENCD beacon bodies themselves. The multi-megabyte transfers from `classicgrand.com` and `modandcrackedapk.com` — the likely installer delivery — rode entirely over TLS, so their content is not recoverable without decryption keys, which are not present in this evidence set.

**Secondary observation (not attributed to this incident)**
The alert log also shows SMBv1/NTLMSSP anomaly signatures and MS-EFSR RPC activity from the victim to the DC (10.11.26.3:139/445). These are informational-severity rules that commonly fire on routine internal Windows SMB/browser-service traffic; nothing in the capture (no unusual payload, no new accounts, no onward lateral movement) ties them to attacker action, so they are noted but not counted as confirmed compromise indicators.
